parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files form one domain-entity module and handle shared rules the same way. Project.ts, Task.ts and User.ts each define one domain entity. All three check required names and titles through the shared requireText helper from value-objects/RequiredText, so that rule lives in one place and is not copied. Task.ts holds its own state rules: markDone throws TaskAlreadyDoneError if the task is already done, matches checks a task against TaskCriteria, and assignTo sets the assignee. Each rule exists in exactly one place. Task uses the module's own value objects (DueDate, TaskStatus) and does not use raw stand-ins for them. Project and User look alike, but neither repeats the other's logic. Both delegate validation to requireText and only change the label passed in. None of the files contains unrelated concerns such as persistence, mapping or DTO shaping.
